s1.syndrome_frame: Sudden onset of oral and skin lesions with abdominal discomfort and difficulty eating, associated with a large renal mass and lymphadenopathy
salient_findings: Sudden warty growths over the lips
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in the axillae, posterior neck, periumbilical region, and groin folds
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms with papillomatous appearance
key_facts: 70-year-old woman
Sudden onset of oral lesions
Difficulty eating
6-month history of vague abdominal discomfort
Extensive papillomatosis over the lips, tongue, and palate
Verrucous, velvety pigmented plaques in multiple areas
Ridged appearance and coarse texture of the palms
Large left-sided renal mass with retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on abdominal CT
Necrotic mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing superior vena cava compression on thorax CT
Invasive carcinoma with focal squamous differentiation on radiologically guided biopsy of renal mass

shortlist.label: Florid cutaneous papillomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the sudden onset of oral and skin lesions

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma with squamous differentiation
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the renal mass and lymphadenopathy on imaging studies

shortlist.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Associates tylosis with oesophageal cancer, but the oral lesions and renal mass are plausible

shortlist.label: Bazex syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Paraneoplastic syndrome with skin lesions, which could explain the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Papillomatosis cutis carcinoides
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition with skin and oral lesions, potentially related to the patient's carcinoma

raw.rationale: The patient's sudden onset of oral lesions, extensive papillomatosis, and characteristic palm lesions are consistent with florid cutaneous papillomatosis, a paraneoplastic syndrome associated with internal malignancies, in this case, the renal mass with urothelial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Urothelial carcinoma with squamous differentiation
rejected.why: While the patient has this type of cancer, it does not directly explain the cutaneous and oral findings.

rejected.label: Howel-Evans syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome is associated with tylosis and esophageal cancer, which are not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Bazex syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome is a paraneoplastic disorder associated with skin lesions, but it is more commonly linked to cancers of the lung, not urothelial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Papillomatosis cutis carcinoides
rejected.why: This condition is associated with carcinoid tumors, which are not indicated in the case.
